title: Zero Trust Network Orchestration Cookbook — RBAC v2, SIEM Mapping, Evidence Automation & mTLS
content:
Purpose
--------
This is a practical cookbook for locking down and operationalizing private deployments (VPC-based, VPC+on-prem agent, or air-gapped). It focuses on: RBAC v2 mappings for orchestration + data plane, a recommended audit-log schema for downstream SIEM ingestion, an evidence-automation runbook to collect and retain artifacts for compliance, and concrete mTLS + firewall hardening patterns. The target audience is SREs, infra engineers, and security reviewers responsible for customer Private deployments.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Redwood Private control plane + customer-managed data plane (VPCs / on-prem).
- Covers network segmentation (zones), host/network firewall templates, mTLS for service-to-service auth, RBAC mapping for operators and automation, audit log format, SIEM mapping, and an automation runbook to collect evidence for audits.
- Not a replacement for regulator-specific policies (we link to those in linked_artifacts).

High-level architecture (textual)
--------------------------------
Components referenced below:
- Control Plane (Redwood-managed): orchestration, model catalog, rollout service (APIs)
- Private Agent (customer-hosted): runtime kernels, healthplane, forwarder
- Management Bastion/Jump host: admin access only
- SIEM Forwarder: local collector (Fluentd/Vector) -> corporate SIEM
- PKI: internal CA + intermediate for mTLS cert issuance

ASCII diagram (linear)
---------------------
[User/Client] -- TLS --> [Public Ingress LB] -- (API calls) --> [Control Plane (Redwood)]
                                             |
                                             +- VPN/Interconnect / Private Peering --> [Customer VPC: Private Agent(s)]
                                                         |
                                                         +- Subnet: compute (gpu-pool)
                                                         +- Subnet: management (bastion, metrics, forwarder)
                                                         +- NACLs + Security Groups (deny-by-default)

RBAC v2: roles and minimal permissions (cookbook)
--------------------------------------------------
Guiding principle: least privilege, role separation, short-lived tokens, and fully-audited service actions. RBAC v2 maps both human roles and machine principals. Examples below are canonical role names used by orchestration and audit tooling.

- role: private-deploy-admin
  description: Full admin for a specific Private deployment instance. Intended for platform security leads (minimal membership).
  allowed_actions: ["deploy:rollback","deploy:promote","config:change","key:rotate"]
  resource_scope: deployment/*

- role: private-deploy-operator
  description: Day-to-day operator for capacity and runtime, cannot change PKI or org-level RBAC.
  allowed_actions: ["instance:restart","pool:scale","logs:read","metrics:read"]
  resource_scope: deployment/<id>/runtime/*

- role: private-deploy-viewer
  description: Read-only; can access dashboards, logs (sanitized) and run diagnostics.
  allowed_actions: ["logs:read","metrics:read","config:view"]
  resource_scope: deployment/<id>

- role: private-deploy-signer (machine)
  description: Short-lived role bound to the internal PKI agent that can request leaf certs for services. Strictly audited.
  allowed_actions: ["cert:issue:leaf"]
  resource_scope: deployment/<id>/pki

RBAC enforcement tips
- Bind roles to ephemeral tokens (1h default) issued by the control plane or customer STS.
- Use attribute-based constraints: allow manager overrides only from specific IP ranges (admin bastion).
- Audit every role assignment/change (magic: create an audit event with request_id and approver_id).

Audit log schema (recommended)
------------------------------
We standardize on a JSON log envelope to make SIEM mapping deterministic. Keep these fields in every event. Example below is a single-line JSON event; we recommend newline-delimited JSON.

Example audit event (single line)
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-10T15:12:04.123Z",
  "event_type": "role_assignment",
  "request_id": "req_9382ab12",
  "actor": "users/jamal.huang@redwoodai.com",
  "actor_id": "u-3912",
  "actor_ip": "203.0.113.42",
  "action": "grant",
  "target_type": "role",
  "target_id": "private-deploy-operator",
  "resource_scope": "deployment/dpl-77a9",
  "outcome": "success",
  "details": "granted by approval workflow #JIRA-1229",
  "signature": "sha256:...",
  "service": "control-plane",
  "region": "us-west-2"
}

Mandatory fields explanation
- timestamp: RFC3339 with ms
- request_id: unique per user action, propagated through system
- actor, actor_id, actor_ip: human or machine principal info
- action: short verb namespace (deploy:scale, cert:issue)
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- signature: HMAC or signing key id for non-repun table proof-of-origin (optional if forwarded by authenticated collector)

SIEM export and ingestion mapping
--------------------------------
Goal: minimize transforms in the SIEM; forward structured JSON. Recommended pipeline: local vector/fluentd -> local buffering -> compress+tls -> SIEM endpoint (Splunk/Elastic/Datadog).

Mapping suggestions (Elastic Common Schema / Splunk friendly)
- ecs.event.dataset = "redwood.private.audit"
- host.name = agent-hostname
- network.direction = inbound|outbound when applicable
- user.name = actor (strip domain if needed)
- event.id = request_id
- event.action = action
- event.outcome = outcome
- file.signature or audit.action_signature = signature
- tags: ["private-deploy", "rbac-v2", "evidence-dot"]

Splunk props example (index-time extraction)
- sourcetype = redwood:private:audit
- props.conf
  - INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS = json
  - KV_MODE = none

Elastic ingest pipeline snippet (pseudocode)
- pipeline: parse json -> rename audit fields to ecs -> tag with deployment_id -> route to warm index

Evidence automation runbook (collect + verify)
------------------------------------------------
Principle: every change that affects control plane, PKI, network configuration, or production data plane must have an automated evidence bundle produced (artifact bundle). The bundle is signed and archived for X days (policy: 1 year for SOC2, 7 years for FedRAMP depending on customer).

Bundle contents (minimum)
- snapshot/firewall-rules.json (aws cli: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters ...)
- vpc-flow-logs-archive.tar.gz (last 24 hours on change window)
- audit-events.ndjson (events with request_id and signature)
- mTLS-certificates-manifest.txt (serial numbers + notAfter + issuer)
- forwarder-config.yaml (vector/fluentd config hash)
- evidence-manifest.json (sha256 list of files + created_at + creator)

Automation steps (scriptable)
1) Trigger: PR merge to infra/ops or config change event.
2) Create unique run id: run-<ts>-<rand>.
3) Collect snapshots using customer-provided automation role (minimal perms):
   - aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filter Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc> --output json > firewall-rules.json
   - aws ec2 describe-network-acls --vpc-id <vpc> > nacls.json
   - aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /aws/vpc/flowlogs --start-time <window> --end-time <window> > vpc-flow.log
4) Pull recent audit-events (control plane + agent) by request_id window and include vector-forwarder checkpoint.
5) Create manifest, sign (artifact-sign tool using private key stored in HSM), upload to secure object storage and emit audit event that bundle created.
6) Notify compliance channel with signed link + bundle metadata.

Retention/rotation policy
- Evidence bundles: 1 year by default for customer audit; escalate retention by contract.
- Audit logs: hot storage 90 days, warm 1 year, cold 7+ years depending on compliance.

Network segmentation and firewall patterns
----------------------------------------
Principles: deny-by-default, minimal egress for compute, strict ingress via LB and bastion only, separate subnets for control/compute/management, host-based firewall as second layer.

Example security group templates (AWS style)
- sg-control-plane-ingress
  inbound: allow TLS 443 from Redwood-ControlPlane-IPs (managed list), allow management from bastion only
  outbound: allow 443 to agent subnets (for webhook/pull)

- sg-agent-runtime
  inbound: allow from private-lb:443, allow healthchecks from monitoring subnets, allow SSH from bastion (port 2200 only)
  outbound: restricted to sandboxed registry, telemetry endpoints, and SIEM forwarder

NACL recommendations
- Stateless deny all ephemeral ports inbound unless explicitly needed for external peering.
- Explicitly allow ephemeral outbound range for agent-to-control-plane calls, but restrict to control-plane IP list.

mTLS configuration and checklist
--------------------------------
Goal: mutual TLS for service-to-service authentication within the data plane; use short-lived certificates and automated rotation.

Checklist
- PKI: Root CA offline, intermediate CA for signing, short-lived leaf certs (TTL <= 24 hours for ephemeral workloads; <= 7 days for long lived infra services).
- CRL/OCSP: provide OCSP responders inside customer network or use signed stapling.
- Cipher suites: disable TLS 1.0/1.1; prefer TLS1.2+ and TLS1.3. Only allow AEAD ciphers (e.g., TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256).
- Certificate fields: SAN must include service identity (service://<deployment>/<service>/<instance>), not IPs as primary identity.
- s_client verification command (example):
  openssl s_client -connect agent-host:8443 -tls1_2 -servername agent-host -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem
  Verify: handshake ok, verify return code: 0
- Heartbeat checks: periodic mutual ping across services with fresh certs to detect stale/expired certs.

Hardening verification tests (automated)
---------------------------------------
- Network tests
  - run-nmap-scan.sh: verify only allowed ports are present from bastion and from public ingress.
  - vpc-firewall-diff: compare current security groups vs approved template; fail if drift > 0.

- PKI tests
  - cert-latency-check: validate cert issuance < 500ms in normal conditions for ephemeral request.
  - cert-expiry-alert: create SIEM rule: if cert.notAfter < now + 72h then create incident.

- Audit integrity
  - audit-chain-checker: verify sequence numbers and signatures for a window of events; if discontinuity detected, escalate.

SIEM queries (examples)
----------------------
- Find failed role grant attempts (Elastic)
  GET /_search?q=event.action:grant AND event.outcome:failure AND ecs.event.dataset: "redwood.private.audit"

- Splunk SPL to find exported evidence bundles older than retention policy
  index=redwood_logs sourcetype=redwood:evidence action=bundle_created | where _time < relative_time(now(), "-365d")

Operational play snippets
-------------------------
- Onboarding a customer VPC: run onboarding script which enforces template SGs, deploys agent as DaemonSet (k8s), configures Vector to forward to corporate SIEM, and registers VPC id in control plane. The script emits an initial evidence bundle and a verification audit event.

- Incident: rotated certs failed to propagate
  1) rollback new cert issuance via control-plane-admin-only path
  2) trigger agent-side reload (graceful restart)
  3) collect evidence bundle (pre-rotation and post-rotation) and attach to incident ticket JIRA-INC-####

Open questions / next iterations
-------------------------------
- Should we standardize on a single certified forwarder (Vector) and provide hardened config? (pros: smaller blast radius; cons: single component to support).
- Evaluate storing signed evidence bundles in customer-owned S3 for customers who require physical custody.
- Automate RBAC change approvals with a PBAC (policy-based access control) engine instead of manual approvals for faster, auditable flows.

References and quick commands
----------------------------
- aws examples: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc>
- openssl: openssl s_client -connect <host>:<port> -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem
- sample audit tail: tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood-audit.ndjson | jq '. | select(.outcome == "failure")'

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This is an operational-first draft; the checklist covers the most common audit items we see in customer reviews and SOC2 questionnaires. Please comment inline on:
  - RBAC role names and scoping semantics (we will convert to formal protobuf schema),
  - retention windows and default values,
  - whether the evidence bundle content meets FedRAMP baseline for our targeted customers.

Change log
----------
- 2025-11-20: initial draft (Ravi)
- 2026-01-12: added SIEM mapping and RBAC action examples (Sofia)
- 2026-03-10: updated audit schema, added signing step and example commands (Jamal)

End of document
